summary: Verified all five Part A docstring defects at their cited lines; measured Parts B/C/D against source. Four premise corrections found: A4 is only half-true (temporalTableau_complete genuinely does not exist), A1 has three defects not one, a sixth unlisted overclaim exists at LJ/Basic.lean:78-79, and Part C's genericity premise is false as stated though its conclusion survives via an in-tree letI precedent.
key_findings: A1 (ConservativeChain.lean:140): 'strictly' unproved (sole strictness hit in tree is the overclaim itself); ALSO 'five' contradicted by its own three-node display block; ALSO chain identity conflates Imp/Int/Prop with the neighbouring Min/Int/Prop theorems.
A2 (Tableau/Classical/DecisionProcedure.lean:23): reproduced. Lines 33-34 of the same header ALSO describe the non-existent instance and must be fixed together, or a dangling description remains.
A3 (Tableau/Intuitionistic/DecisionProcedure.lean:62): confirmed zero consumers outside Cslib/Logics/Propositional/ across Cslib/ and CslibTests/.

A4 PREMISE CORRECTION: 'do not exist yet for either calculus' is FALSE for intuitionistic but STILL TRUE for temporal. temporalTableau_complete does not exist as a declaration; it appears only in Temporal/Tableau/Completeness.lean:122 as a blocked obligation. Re-tensing must be SPLIT, not blanket.

A6 NEW (not in task): LJ/Basic.lean:78-79 claims cut elimination and the subformula property are 'proved once generically over T'. Both are at IPL only. Same defect class as A1-A5, and it is the exact claim Part C would rely on.
B1 confirmed near-exact LK template; only difference is lj_iff_ivalid's explicit IValid.{u,u} universe pin.
B2 confirmed no new proof needed; the one real decision is public API shape (recommend bundled CutFreeXProof wrapper over un-privatising the core).

B3 estimate corrected: listToImp/ctxToImp reusable as claimed, but the four lj*Deduction* helpers are LJ-specific. They touch no gated constructor, so generalising them is mechanical and should be shared with C1 rather than duplicated. Task 614 (computable ctxToImp) is live and [researching].

C1 PREMISE CORRECTION: ljCutAdmissibility is NOT generic over T -- no {T : Theory Atom} binder anywhere in LJ/CutElimination.lean (56 LJProof mentions vs 15 mostly-projection SeqProof mentions). BUT the conclusion survives: SeqProof.mono (Basic.lean:184-186) already solves the only hard part (reconstructing the [IsIntuitionistic T]-gated botL via letI instance rebind), and Basic.lean:178-179 documents that idiom. Five .botL reconstruction sites need it. Highest-risk spot is the decreasing_by at LJ/CutElimination.lean:650 referencing the IPL-only LJProof.height re-export.
C2 task claim confirmed: SeqProof.formulas IS generic; the subformula PROPERTY theorems are not.

D1 confirmed orImp is the only one of eight fragments with zero completeness theorem. Splits into D1-relative (under 10 lines, composing the existing hilbertIplConservativeOverOrImp_iff biconditional with IPL completeness -- recommend IN scope) and D1-absolute (needs a new algebra class for the meet-free imp-disjunction signature -- recommend OUT of scope, own research task).

D2 DIFFICULTY OVERSTATED: the decide/WellFounded.fix concern is a red herring. CslibTests/ModalFrameSeparation.lean already establishes an analogous separation by hand-built semantic countermodels ported as named theorems, explicitly routing around the same kernel stall. MPL != IPL is nearly free (~15-25 lines) via a Unit model with bf := True, cheap precisely because LM/Soundness.lean:61 quantifies over arbitrary upward-closed bot_forces. IPL != CPL is ~30-50 lines via the two-point Kripke chain. Recommend as a separate follow-up task, scoped at roughly one phase, NOT as an open research problem.

D2 CAVEAT: both separations would establish MPL < IPL < CPL, which is NOT the Imp -> Int -> Prop chain A1's docstring displays. A1's 'strictly' must be corrected now and must not be reinstated on the strength of D2 alone.
G6: agree it is a judgment call, but note it is coupled to A2 -- A2 deletes the docstring entry for exactly the instance G6 would create. Recommend deciding both as one question.
G9: agree architectural and fine; recommend a module-docstring note in NaturalDeduction/Equivalence.lean, since undocumented deliberate absences generate future false coverage findings.

recommended_phases.content: C1 generalise cut elimination to T; instantiate at MPL
D1-relative orImp completeness vs IPL semantics

out_of_scope_recommend_spawn: D1-absolute: fragment-matched algebraic completeness for the imp-disjunction fragment; needs its own research pass on the algebra class.
D2: the two separation theorems (MPL != IPL, IPL != CPL); tractable at roughly one phase but is new mathematical content and should not be mixed into a cleanup diff.
open_decisions_for_planner: B2 public API shape: bundled CutFreeXProof wrapper (recommended) vs un-privatising maeharaCore/ljMaeharaCore.
Whether A2 is a plain deletion or is paired with building the G6 Fintype-free tableau instance.
Whether B3 waits on task 614's computable ctxToImp (recommend not blocking; accept the noncomputable taint with an explicit note if 614 has not landed).
risks: Phase 4 (C1) is the only phase with real risk of not completing as written. The risk is mechanical, not mathematical: termination checking under a new {T} binder, specifically LJ/CutElimination.lean:650's decreasing_by referencing LJProof.height. If it stalls, mark that phase [BLOCKED] with the goal state recorded; phases 5-7 depend on it, but phases 1-3 and 8 are independent and can still land.

zero_debt.notes: No sorry occurs anywhere under Cslib/Logics/Propositional/ (all grep hits are docstring prose). intuitionisticTableau_decides verifies with axioms {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}.
